sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: This chapter describes the materials and construction methods used for soil nail walls. The information is intended to familiarize design engineers with materials available and construction procedures commonly employed. Understanding construction methods and materials is essential for developing realistic designs and specifications. The chapter covers soil nail components (tendons, connection hardware, grout), construction methods (drilling, grouting, facing), and alternate materials and methods.

sections.title: Soil Nail Wall Components
sections.body: The primary components of a soil nail wall include: (a) Tendons: solid steel bars conforming to ASTM A615 Grade 60 (fy = 420 MPa) or Grade 75 (fy = 520 MPa), or ASTM A722 Grade 150 (fy = 1035 MPa). Common diameters are #6 (19 mm) through #10 (32 mm). Hollow bars (self-drilling) are also used, conforming to ASTM A615 or proprietary specifications. (b) Connection components: bearing plates (typically 200x200x19 mm), hex nuts, washers, beveled washers for inclined nails, and headed studs for connecting to final facing. (c) Grout: neat cement grout with minimum 28-day compressive strength of 21 MPa (3,000 psi), water-cement ratio of 0.40-0.50. Grout serves to transfer loads between the nail and surrounding soil, and provides corrosion protection to the tendon.

sections.title: Construction Methods
sections.body: Construction methods include: (a) Drilling: rotary or percussion drilling methods with or without casing, depending on ground conditions. Open-hole drilling is preferred in stable soils; cased drilling required in collapsible or flowing ground. Typical drill hole diameters are 100-200 mm (4-8 in). (b) Grouting: tremie method from bottom of hole upward using neat cement grout. Gravity grouting is standard; pressure grouting may increase bond in marginal soils. (c) Shotcrete facing: dry-mix or wet-mix process, typically 75-100 mm thick for initial facing. WWM (typically W1.4 x W1.4 or W2.0 x W2.0, 100x100 mm grid) provides reinforcement. (d) Centralizers: placed at regular intervals (typically every 2.5 m) to ensure minimum grout cover around the tendon. (e) Final facing: CIP reinforced concrete (150-200 mm) or additional shotcrete layer, applied after all excavation and nailing is complete.
key_points: Drilling: rotary or percussion, 100-200 mm diameter holes
Open-hole in stable soils; cased drilling in collapsible ground
Grouting: tremie from bottom up, neat cement grout
Pressure grouting may increase bond in marginal soils
Initial shotcrete facing: 75-100 mm thick, dry or wet mix

sections.title: Drainage Systems
sections.body: Drainage is critical for soil nail wall performance. Typical drainage provisions include: (a) geocomposite strip drains (prefabricated drainage panels) installed vertically behind the facing between nail rows, typically 300 mm wide; (b) a continuous toe drain (perforated pipe in gravel-filled trench) at the base of the wall to collect and convey water; (c) weep holes through the facing at regular intervals (typically 1.5-3 m spacing) to relieve hydrostatic pressure; and (d) surface water collection systems (ditches, swales) above the wall crest to prevent water from infiltrating behind the wall. Inadequate drainage is a common cause of soil nail wall distress and failure.

sections.title: Alternate Materials and Methods
sections.body: Alternate materials and methods include: (a) sculpted or architectural facings for aesthetic applications using form liners or sculpted shotcrete; (b) hollow bar soil nails (HBSN, also called self-drilling nails) that combine drilling and grouting into a single operation, reducing construction time. HBSN use a sacrificial drill bit and are grouted through the hollow bar during drilling. They are particularly useful in collapsing ground where open-hole methods are difficult. (c) Fiberglass or FRP nails for temporary applications where the nails must be cut through by future tunnel boring machines. (d) Launched soil nails driven pneumatically without drilling for temporary applications in appropriate soils.
